2/ Canada is simultaneously one of America’s biggest customers, suppliers, investors, energy providers, agricultural markets, and manufacturing partners. Through June 2026, it was our second-largest goods export market and second-largest source of imports.

3/ Our economies are so closely connected that the Administration exempted energy and critical minerals from its Section 338 tariffs. In 2023, Canada sent 97% of its crude-oil exports to the United States, and Canadian crude supplied roughly 24% of U.S. refinery throughput.

4/ That exemption demonstrates the broader point, the interconnection of our economies. American manufacturers depend on Canadian metals, lumber, machinery, and components, and tariffs on those inputs make American-made goods more expensive and less competitive.

5/ For more than a decade, Canada has been the largest export market for American-made passenger vehicles and light trucks. From April 2025 through March 2026, Canadian imports of U.S. motor vehicles fell 22%, or $5.6 billion, compared with the same period a year earlier.
